method: Per-pool web research; every cited page was opened during research. status: verified | needs-research | rejected. Lead-auditor overrides and owner rulings (2026-11-09) are applied in data/character-abilities.js.

ownerRulings.giants: about 8 ft or taller, with a documented size
ownerRulings.stealth: needs a stealth/invisibility feat; a role or title is not enough
ownerRulings.tech: advanced/powered armor counts (Iron Man, War Machine); standard-issue armor does not

records.name: Spider-Man
records.feat: Wears Stark-built suits; in Avengers: Infinity War Tony Stark gives him the nanotech Iron Spider armor, which deploys from a pod and has four AI-controlled spider-leg pincers, its own oxygen supply and upgraded web-shooters.
records.continuity: MCU: Spider-Man: Homecoming (2017); Avengers: Infinity War (2018)
records.limitation: Stark-built suits (Homecoming suit, Iron Spider armor)

records.name: Star-Lord
records.feat: Uses jet boot attachments for short bursts of flight, e.g. escaping Morag and during the Battle of Xandar in Guardians of the Galaxy (2014), and firing on Thanos' army from the air in Endgame; also pilots the Milano under fire from Korath on Morag.
records.continuity: MCU: Guardians of the Galaxy (2014); Avengers: Endgame (2019)
records.limitation: Flight via jet boots / later Aero-Rig; ship piloting

records.name: Star-Lord
records.feat: Relies on gadgets: jet boot attachments for flight and a deployable helmet/mask that lets him survive in space (e.g. outside the Kyln), plus his M-ship the Milano.

records.name: Mantis
records.feat: Empath who senses and alters emotions through touch; in Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 2 she puts Ego to sleep during the battle at his core, and in Infinity War she sedates Thanos on Titan.
records.continuity: MCU: Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 2 (2017); Avengers: Infinity War (2018)

records.name: Nebula
records.feat: A cyborg whose body Thanos rebuilt with machinery: a cybernetic left arm (electroshock, grappling hook), a bionic eye, and a synaptic memory drive that replays recordings, a key plot point in Endgame.
records.continuity: MCU: Guardians of the Galaxy (2014) through Avengers: Endgame (2019)

records.name: Nebula
records.feat: Pilots spacecraft in combat: takes over a Ravager M-Ship to flee the Dark Aster in Guardians of the Galaxy (2014), fights Gamora from an M-Ship in Vol. 2, and crashes a Necrocraft into Thanos on Titan in Infinity War.
records.continuity: MCU: Guardians of the Galaxy (2014); Vol. 2 (2017); Avengers: Infinity War (2018)

records.name: Yondu
records.feat: Controls his Yaka Arrow with whistles through a cybernetic controller implanted in his head (it glows red when in use); in Vol. 2 he must get his prototype fin back to escape Taserface's mutiny.
records.continuity: MCU: Guardians of the Galaxy (2014); Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 2 (2017)
records.limitation: Arrow control requires the head-fin controller

records.name: Yondu
records.feat: In the Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 2 finale he flies Quill to safety from the exploding Ego using a flight rig; earlier he rides the Yaka Arrow down to Ego's surface ('Mary Poppins'). He also pilots an M-Ship in the Battle of Xandar.
records.continuity: MCU: Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 2 (2017)
records.note: Wiki calls it a flight suit; not a jetpack per se (Rocket's Aero-Rig).

records.name: Rocket
records.feat: Skilled combat pilot: flies an M-Ship against the Dark Aster and crashes the Ravager Warbird into it during the Battle of Xandar (GotG 2014), dodges the Sovereign fleet through an asteroid field in Vol. 2, and pilots the Benatar in Infinity War.
records.continuity: MCU: Guardians of the Galaxy (2014); Vol. 2 (2017); Avengers: Infinity War (2018)
records.note: He flew an M-Ship/Warbird at Xandar, not the Milano.

records.name: Winter Soldier
records.feat: Bucky's HYDRA-fitted cybernetic metal arm, described as 'the highest level of weaponized technology', blocks Captain America's shield and crushes steel; Wakanda later gives him a vibranium replacement arm (Infinity War).
records.continuity: MCU: Captain America: The Winter Soldier (2014); Civil War (2016); Avengers: Infinity War (2018)
records.note: Counts under 'cyborg/advanced technology': the arm is an advanced weaponized cybernetic limb, not mere armor.

records.name: Killmonger
records.feat: Wears the golden Wakandan nanotech Panther Habit stored in a necklace; its vibranium absorbs kinetic energy and releases it as a pulse that throws back the Dora Milaje, until the maglev's sonic stabilizers disrupt it in the final fight.
records.limitation: Only while wearing the Panther Habit

records.name: Valkyrie
records.feat: Rides her winged steed Warsong into the Battle of Earth in Avengers: Endgame; in Thor: Ragnarok she pilots the Commodore in the escape from Sakaar, and the Valkyrie flashback shows them riding winged horses against Hela.
records.limitation: Winged mount or ship, not unaided flight

records.name: Heimdall
records.feat: In Avengers: Infinity War he uses dark magic to summon the Bifrost one last time, sending Hulk from the Statesman to the New York Sanctum on Earth.

records.name: Heimdall
records.feat: In Thor: Ragnarok, Heimdall shares his sight with Thor across realms; Thor's eyes glow like Heimdall's as he sees Asgard from Sakaar. He is also all-seeing across the Nine Realms.

records.name: Gorr the God Butcher
records.feat: The All-Black Necrosword lets him move through shadows into the Shadow Realm, vanishing and reappearing for surprise attacks, e.g. appearing behind Valkyrie to stab her in Thor: Love and Thunder.

records.name: Thanos
records.feat: With the Space Stone in Avengers: Infinity War he teleports from Knowhere to Vormir with Gamora and to Wakanda, and opens a portal to pull himself and the Black Order off the Statesman.
records.limitation: Requires the Space Stone / Infinity Gauntlet

records.name: Electro
records.feat: His body becomes pure electrical energy and nearly weightless; in Spider-Man: No Way Home he hovers above the power lines while drawing energy from them on arrival in the forest.
records.note: Wiki lists flight as a power; only the power-line hover is described as a scene.

records.name: Sandman
records.feat: During the Liberty Island battle in Spider-Man: No Way Home, a gigantic Sandman chases a Spider-Man through the Statue of Liberty scaffolding; he enlarges by absorbing sand.
records.limitation: Giant sand form; needs sand to absorb

records.name: Kang the Conqueror
records.feat: A normal human whose power comes from his technology: in Ant-Man and the Wasp: Quantumania his suit boosts his strength and fires concussive energy blasts, and he needs his ship's power core repaired to escape the Quantum Realm.
records.continuity: MCU: Ant-Man and the Wasp: Quantumania (2023)
records.note: MCU wiki armor page also lists force fields and energy blasts: https://marvelcinematicuniverse.fandom.com/wiki/Kang_the_Conqueror%27s_Armor

records.name: Ego
records.feat: Ego is a living planet, which he says is 'no smaller than Earth's moon'; his humanoid form is an avatar, and in Vol. 2 he shapes matter into a giant duplicate of himself.
records.continuity: MCU: Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 2 (2017)

records.name: Obadiah Stane
records.feat: Builds and wears the Iron Monger armor, reverse-engineered from Tony's Mark I, and fights Iron Man in it in Los Angeles. It flies until it ices over in the upper atmosphere.
records.limitation: Only in the Iron Monger armor

records.name: Ghost
records.feat: Ava Starr wears a S.H.I.E.L.D.-developed Ghost Suit that lets her switch between intangible and solid states at will and manages her quantum condition in Ant-Man and the Wasp.

records.name: Janet van Dyne
records.feat: Hank Pym built her a Wasp suit with four insect-like wings that let her fly fast and nimbly on S.H.I.E.L.D. missions, as seen in the Ant-Man films' flashbacks. Two wings were lost during her 30 years in the Quantum Realm.
records.continuity: MCU: Ant-Man (2015) & Ant-Man and the Wasp (2018) flashbacks
records.limitation: Wasp suit; not able to fly after returning from the Quantum Realm

records.name: Captain Marvel
records.feat: In The Marvels, Carol Danvers, Monica Rambeau and Kamala Khan become quantum-entangled. Whenever they use their light-based powers at the same time they instantly switch places across space, and they learn to coordinate the swaps as a team.
records.limitation: Only while entangled with the other two in The Marvels; swaps places rather than free teleport
records.note: Initially involuntary. Wiki says they learn to coordinate but doesn't explicitly call it deliberate teleportation. Owner may want to judge whether 'swap' counts.

records.name: Ms. Marvel
records.feat: In The Marvels, Carol Danvers, Monica Rambeau and Kamala Khan become quantum-entangled. Whenever they use their light-based powers at the same time they instantly switch places across space, and they learn to coordinate the swaps as a team.
records.limitation: Only while entangled with the other two in The Marvels; swaps places rather than free teleport
records.note: Initially involuntary. Wiki says they learn to coordinate but doesn't explicitly call it deliberate teleportation. Owner may want to judge whether 'swap' counts.

records.name: Monica Rambeau
records.feat: In The Marvels, Carol Danvers, Monica Rambeau and Kamala Khan become quantum-entangled. Whenever they use their light-based powers at the same time they instantly switch places across space, and they learn to coordinate the swaps as a team.
records.limitation: Only while entangled with the other two in The Marvels; swaps places rather than free teleport
records.note: Initially involuntary. Wiki says they learn to coordinate but doesn't explicitly call it deliberate teleportation. Owner may want to judge whether 'swap' counts.

records.name: Ms. Marvel
records.note: MCU Kamala makes giant hard-light fists and enlarges limbs/armor, but there is no full-body growth. Enlarged fists alone don't meet 'becomes enormous'.

records.name: The Watcher
records.note: Wiki (Uatu) and Wikipedia describe no size/giant scale; a fetched episode-8 article applies 'giant' to Ultron, not the Watcher. Would need a specific on-screen scale scene.

records.name: Iron Fist
records.feat: Can heal others by channelling chi into his hands. In Iron Fist season 1 ('The Mistress of All Agonies') Bakuto teaches him to burn away the poison killing Colleen Wing, and the effort knocks Danny out.
records.limitation: Heals others via chi; self-healing not established
records.note: Scene confirmed by TV Tropes recap: https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Recap/IronFist2017S1E9TheMistressOfAllAgonies

records.name: Abomination
records.feat: After his transformation in The Incredible Hulk (2008), Blonsky's body is larger than Hulk's, with his spine protruding from his back. That puts him above the Hulk, who is already tagged giants.
records.note: Size question: MCU Hulk is roughly 8.5-9 ft (fortressofsolitude.co.za). If Hulk qualifies as giants, Abomination (bigger than Hulk) must too.

records.name: Smart Hulk
records.feat: Banner's Smart Hulk form in Avengers: Endgame is the Hulk body with Banner's mind. Avengers-era Hulk is estimated at about 8 ft 5 in, the same scale that earns Hulk his giants tag.
records.note: Consistency call: the MCU wiki says Smart Hulk is somewhat smaller than Savage Hulk. If the owner decides ~8 ft isn't 'giant', drop Hulk's giants tag too.

records.name: Smart Hulk
records.continuity: MCU: Avengers: Endgame (2019); She-Hulk: Attorney at Law (2022)
records.note: Counter-evidence: Smart Hulk's arm, injured by the Snap in Endgame, never healed by itself. In She-Hulk ep 1 he needed an inhibitor and then Jen's synthesized blood to 'completely heal his arm'. No positive regeneration scene found for the Smart Hulk form.

records.name: Green Goblin
records.feat: In Spider-Man: No Way Home he flies a Goblin Glider that he also uses as a weapon (impaling May, wrecking Doc Ock's tentacle) and throws explosive Pumpkin Bombs, one of which destroys the Macchina di Kadavus.

records.name: Ego
records.feat: In Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 2 Ego uses telekinesis to collapse rock formations and move structures, and can hypnotise a victim with a touch to the forehead.
records.continuity: MCU: Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 2 (2017)

records.name: The Watcher
records.feat: In What If...? Uatu moves people between universes and his Observational Plane, e.g. sending Captain Carter home and transporting Black Widow to a new universe.

records.name: The Watcher
records.feat: Uses telekinesis in What If...?, e.g. knocking Jun-Fan's attackers off a train.

records.name: Janet van Dyne
records.feat: Powered by quantum energy, she reverses Ghost's quantum displacement in Ant-Man and the Wasp and clears Hank Pym's mind of the Quantum Realm's effects.
records.limitation: Quantum-energy powers gained in the Quantum Realm

records.name: Janet van Dyne
records.feat: Wore the original Wasp suit Hank Pym built, with Pym Particle shrinking and four artificial wings, on S.H.I.E.L.D. missions.
records.continuity: MCU: Ant-Man (2015) & Ant-Man and the Wasp (2018) flashbacks

records.name: Ant-Man
records.feat: Scott Lang wears Hank Pym's Ant-Man Suit: Pym Particles for shrinking, a protective helmet, and an EMP communication device in the helmet that mimics pheromones so he can command ants.

records.name: The Wasp
records.feat: Hope van Dyne's Wasp Suit, built by Hank Pym, has Pym Particle size manipulation, four wings for flight up to 125 mph, and 'Stinger' gauntlet blasters that can blast through stone.

records.name: Hawkeye
records.feat: Uses signature trick arrows (Putty, Plunger, Explosion, Acid, Smoke Bomb, Pym, USB, etc.) with Kate Bishop during the car chase in Hawkeye episode 3, 'Echoes'.

records.name: Nebula
records.feat: Her cybernetic left arm generates electricity: it fires electroshock blasts, and she uses it to power a damaged Ravager ship.
records.continuity: MCU: Guardians of the Galaxy films; Avengers: Endgame

records.name: Sandman
records.feat: Can turn into a sandstorm and travel long distances through the air. In No Way Home he draws sand from everywhere to form a massive sandstorm after Electro's blast.

records.name: Gorr the God Butcher
records.note: Wiki says the Necrosword grants a regenerative healing factor, but I found no specific on-screen healing scene.

records.name: Electro
records.note: Wiki lists teleportation by dissolving into electricity; no specific scene confirmed.

records.name: Uncle Iroh
records.feat: Master firebender known as the Dragon of the West. In 'The Crossroads of Destiny' he blasts fire to escape the Dai Li with Zuko, and in 'Sozin's Comet, Part 3' he breathes a ring of fire and blasts through Ba Sing Se's Inner Wall.
records.note: The campaign tag is filed under 'Iroh' but the roster name is 'Uncle Iroh'. Re-key the tag to 'Uncle Iroh' or the pick will keep failing.

records.name: Squidward
records.feat: A sea creature (giant Pacific octopus, per 'Feral Friends') who lives in a moai house in undersea Bikini Bottom between SpongeBob and Patrick.
records.note: The tag data uses 'Squidward Tentacles' but the roster name is 'Squidward'. Re-key it.

records.name: Katara
records.feat: Waterbending master: she duels Master Pakku and freezes Zuko under the full moon in the Siege of the North, forms water whips against Zuko in the Crystal Catacombs, and learns to pull water from the air from Hama.

records.name: Aang
records.feat: He flies on his Air Nomad glider staff, airbending wind to take off and stay aloft, including flying alone to confront Fire Lord Ozai.
records.limitation: Airbending-powered glider staff; not unaided flight

records.name: Aang
records.feat: Learns waterbending from Master Pakku in 'The Waterbending Master'. In 'The Siege of the North, Part 2' he merges with the Ocean Spirit La and wipes out the Fire Nation fleet.

records.name: Aang
records.feat: 'The Storm' flashback: after falling into the sea in a storm, he enters the Avatar State and freezes himself inside the iceberg he is later found in.
records.limitation: Shown feat is in the Avatar State; regular icebending is mostly Katara's on screen

records.name: Raphael
records.feat: Trained by Splinter in ninjutsu. The wiki says he moves around New York undetected and hides in shadows unnoticed. This is the same evidence that qualifies Leonardo and Donatello.
records.continuity: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (1987 animated series)
records.note: The wiki gives a general skill description and names no single episode, the same standard as the already-granted Leonardo and Donatello entries.

records.name: Michelangelo
records.feat: Called an expert in ninjutsu who could move about New York City undetected and hide in shadows.
records.continuity: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (1987 animated series)
records.note: General skill description; no single episode named. Same standard as Leonardo and Donatello.

records.name: Donatello
records.feat: The team's inventor: he built the Turtle Van, Turtle Communicators, Turtle Blimp and a working inter-dimensional portal. In 'Turtles Forever' he makes the Trans-dimensional Portal Stick.
records.continuity: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (1987 animated series)

records.name: Megatron
records.feat: A Cybertronian, one of the Decepticons' 'villainous faction of alien robots', who transforms into vehicles or weapons. His 1984 G1 form is a Walther P38 handgun.
records.note: The roster line only says 'Decepticon leader'. G1 is assumed because Optimus Prime is listed as 'Autobot leader'.

records.name: Megatron
records.feat: In the G1 cartoon the Decepticons, Megatron included, fly in robot mode. In 'War Dawn' Orion Pax watches the Decepticons fly, 'an ability no-one else has'.
records.note: Source is a fan-site article; tfwiki.net blocks fetching. Later continuities (2007 film jet, Revenge of the Fallen flying tank) also fly, so the tag holds whichever version is meant.

records.name: Plankton
records.feat: A planktonic copepod who lives and runs the Chum Bucket in undersea Bikini Bottom.

records.name: Plankton
records.feat: Built his computer wife Karen. He uses mind-control bucket helmets in The SpongeBob SquarePants Movie, unleashes the Duplicatotron 3000 robot army in Battle for Bikini Bottom, and pilots robot suits and mechs.

records.name: Marvin the Martian
records.feat: Uses the Illudium Q-36 Explosive Space Modulator in his attempts to blow up Earth (called the Uranium PU-36 in 'Haredevil Hare'), and carries a ray gun in nearly every appearance.

records.name: Marvin the Martian
records.feat: In 'The Hasty Hare' (1952), as Commander of Flying Saucer X-2, he pilots his saucer to Earth and back.

records.name: Wile E. Coyote
records.feat: His whole method is mail-order Acme gadgets. In 'Fast and Furry-ous' (1949) he uses a rocket, the Acme Super Outfit, an improvised snow-maker and Fleet-Feet Jet-Propelled Tennis Shoes.
records.continuity: Looney Tunes: Wile E. Coyote and the Road Runner shorts
records.note: Borderline: the tech is cartoon-mail-order rather than advanced. It still fits 'signature gadgets' (rockets, jet shoes), which define the character.

records.name: Hercules
records.feat: Rides the winged horse Pegasus. Against the Hydra he whistles for Pegasus and slices off a head while flying around it.

records.name: Moana
records.feat: Chosen by the ocean, which repeatedly carries and rescues her. The wiki notes she swims naturally and stays underwater unusually long. She dives for the heart of Te Fiti, and in Moana 2 dives to touch Motufetu.
records.note: She cannot bend water herself (the wiki says so explicitly). The tag rests on her ocean bond and underwater feats.

records.name: Elastigirl
records.feat: In The Incredibles she flies a borrowed jet to Nomanisan Island and shoots down missiles before it is hit. In Incredibles 2 she flies a helicopter escorting the ambassador.
records.note: The wiki also lists gliding via a self-made wingsuit shape, but ties it to no scene.

records.name: Rick Sanchez
records.feat: Flies his space cruiser, often drunk. The Pilot episode opens with him flying it with Morty.

records.name: Morty
records.feat: Uses portal technology himself: he opens a portal to the Prime Dimension with Rick C-131's portal gun, uses Rick's gun to fix damage across the galaxy, and in 'Forgetting Sarick Mortshall' makes working portal fluid.

records.name: WALL-E
records.feat: In WALL-E (2008) he grabs a fire extinguisher as he escapes the exploding pod and uses it to propel himself through space around the Axiom with EVE.
records.limitation: Propelled by a fire extinguisher; one scene
records.note: Source is a University of Leicester student-physics journal analysing the scene. Wikipedia confirms he grabs the extinguisher.

records.name: Sandy Cheeks
records.feat: Scientist and inventor who built her treedome, air suit and helmet. She also invents a rocket ('Sandy's Rocket'), a teleporter, a shrinking submarine, a robot and the Protogenerator 2000 cloner ('Overbooked').

records.name: Edna Mode
records.feat: She designs high-tech supersuits (a homing device in Mr. Incredible's suit, a sensor suit for Jack-Jack), and her home uses similar high-end tech.
records.note: She makes the tech for others; no source shows her personally relying on gadgets or armor. Designer is a job title, so this is the owner's call. Leaning no.

records.name: Stitch
records.feat: Uses a Mark I Plasma Blaster, first after crash-landing in Hawaii in the 2002 film. In the series, Jumba's blaster is his main weapon against other experiments.
records.continuity: Disney's Lilo & Stitch (2002) and Lilo & Stitch: The Series
records.note: He is a genetic experiment, not a robot; the tag rests on the blaster.

records.name: Stitch
records.feat: In Lilo & Stitch (2002) he steals a red police cruiser and engages its hyperdrive to escape the Galactic Federation fleet.

records.name: Buzz Lightyear
records.feat: Toy Story (1995): he cannot really fly, but after the rocket launch he pops his wings and 'falls with style' (glides) into Andy's family car.
records.limitation: Glide only; unaided flight attempts fail (breaks his arm at Sid's house)
records.note: Dispute check: this is the Toy Story toy (roster: 'To infinity and beyond'). The tag holds only because the brief counts gliding. Record kind=glide, not self-flight.

records.name: SpongeBob SquarePants
records.feat: The wiki lists regeneration: he can quickly regrow injured or removed body parts. His detachable limbs appear in 'Big Pink Loser' and 'Graveyard Shift', and he buds clones in 'Pressure'.
records.note: Dispute check: upheld, though the wiki names no episode for the regrowth itself.

records.name: Patrick Star
records.feat: In 'Karate Star' he tears off his own arm and a new Patrick grows from it. He later explains that starfish regrow their arms.
records.note: Dispute check: upheld.

records.name: Aang
records.feat: Takes Zuko as his firebending teacher, and the two undergo the Sun Warrior trial before the dragons Ran and Shaw ('The Firebending Masters'). He firebends against Ozai in the finale.
records.note: Dispute check: upheld.

records.name: Blossom
records.feat: In 'Ice Sore' (1999) she discovers her ice breath during a heat wave and uses it to freeze a flaming meteor headed for Townsville.
records.note: Dispute check: upheld. Episode details from the TV Tropes recap: https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Recap/ThePowerpuffGirlsS1E8PasteMakesWasteIceSore

records.name: Aang
records.feat: In 'The Siege of the North, Part 2' he merges with the Ocean Spirit La, becoming a massive glowing koi spirit that wipes out the Fire Nation invaders.
records.limitation: Only while merged with the Ocean Spirit (one episode)

records.name: Mickey Mouse
records.feat: In Fantasia's 'The Sorcerer's Apprentice' he uses his master's magic to bring a broom to life, and cannot control it.
records.limitation: Borrowed sorcerer's magic; uncontrolled; one segment
records.note: Roster tagline is Mickey Mouse Clubhouse, but the roster entry is the general Mickey character.

records.name: Daffy Duck
records.feat: As Duck Dodgers in 'Duck Dodgers in the 24½th Century' (1953), he sets off by rocket with his cadet, flies past the lettered planets and reaches Planet X.
records.continuity: Looney Tunes: Duck Dodgers in the 24½th Century (1953)
records.note: The source says he travels by rocket; it does not spell out who is at the controls.

records.name: Pa Gorg
records.feat: One of the Gorgs, whom the Muppet Wiki calls 'the giant characters of Fraggle Rock' (the same species as Junior Gorg, who already qualifies).

records.name: Ma Gorg
records.feat: One of the Gorgs, 'the giant characters of Fraggle Rock', the same giant species as Junior Gorg.

records.name: Abby Cadabby
records.feat: Fairy-in-training who casts wand spells ('Zippity-zap!'), including turning things into pumpkins. In her Season 37 debut her wand sets off too much lightning and breaks.

records.name: Abby Cadabby
records.feat: Floats when she is happy, and stars in the animated 'Abby's Flying Fairy School' (Season 40).
records.note: The page does not mention wings; the flight evidence is floating and the fairy-school flying.

records.name: Abby Cadabby
records.feat: Pops in and out of thin air; when asked to go home she says she's 'gotta poof'.

records.name: Sweetums
records.feat: A 'large, hairy ogre who towers above his human and Muppet co-stars', called 'the huge monster' next to Robin.
records.note: No height is given and no source calls him a giant; he towers above the cast, as Thog (9½ ft, already granted giants) does. Needs an owner size threshold.

records.name: Big Bird
records.feat: Canonically 8'2" tall. In a 1985 Toronto Star interview quoted on Muppet Wiki he calls himself 'a giant golden condor'.
records.note: The word 'giant' comes from Big Bird's own in-character self-description; the wiki narration just gives 8'2". He cannot fly (says his grandpa was an emu).

records.name: Mr. Snuffleupagus
records.feat: Weighs 1,000 pounds (Episode 1606), has a 65 triple-G shoe size, and the wiki calls the costume 'enormous'.
records.note: Huge, but no source calls him giant. Owner size-threshold call.

records.name: Big Mean Carl
records.feat: A shaggy monster with a voracious appetite who eats game-show contestants on 'Swift Wits'.
records.note: The source gives no size and never calls him giant; he wants to grow as big as his 'much bigger brother'. Leaning no.

records.name: Link Hogthrob
records.feat: Captain of the spaceship Swinetrek in 'Pigs in Space'. He works the ship's controls himself in episode 205 ('Mid-Course Correction', pressing the wrong navigation button) and episode 209 ('The Captain's Controls').
records.continuity: The Muppet Show: Pigs in Space
records.note: Comedic and incompetent piloting, but demonstrated at the controls, not just a title.

records.name: Dr. Bunsen Honeydew
records.feat: Muppet Labs inventor (gorilla detector, banana sharpener, exploding clothes). In The Muppet Movie his Insta-Grow pills enlarge Animal to scare off Doc Hopper; in Muppets from Space he invents devices to rescue Gonzo.
records.continuity: The Muppet Show / The Muppet Movie (1979) / Muppets from Space (1999)

records.name: Grover
records.feat: As his superhero alter ego Super Grover he flies, though he often crash-lands on other characters (Elmo's World and many street segments).
records.limitation: Only as Super Grover; frequent crash landings

records.name: The Amazing Mumford
records.feat: His spells genuinely work, with chaotic results: he turns himself and Leslie into rabbits (Ep. 1447), turns Gladys the Cow into a duck (Ep. 2579), and makes Thumbelina big but shrinks Kermit (Ep. 2696).

records.name: Marjory the Trash Heap
records.feat: The Fraggles' oracle, who 'knows all and sees all'. She hands out 'magic' items, and the wiki credits her with apparent powers to teleport objects or Fraggles and communicate telepathically.
records.note: The wiki notes her advice is often practical rather than magical, but credits genuine teleport/telepathy powers; no episode named for those.

records.name: Cantus
records.feat: Plays a magic pipe that only makes songs for a Fraggle in touch with their inner song; his playing makes nearby flowers burst into bloom.

records.name: Little Bird
records.feat: Shown flying on Sesame Street; Muppet Wiki notes marionette versions of Little Bird are often used for his flying scenes.

records.name: Bernice
records.feat: Bert's pet pigeon.
records.note: The source never shows her flying (its only flying reference is a different bird). Not confirmed.

records.name: Hoots the Owl
records.feat: His backstory says he 'flew downtown', where he got into jazz.
records.note: Backstory wording only (possibly figurative); no on-screen flight found.

records.name: Sam Eagle
records.feat: Stern patriotic eagle of The Muppet Show.
records.note: No source found showing him fly; Wikipedia mentions no flight, and Muppet Wiki's page would not load. Being a bird is not evidence.

records.name: Slimey the Worm
records.feat: Passed WASA's 'stickability' test to become one of five 'astro-worms' on a 1998 moon mission story arc, running weightless experiments and collecting samples.

records.feat: Uses rocket boots to reach an overhang near the Jedi Temple roof during the holocron heist and to save himself after Fennec kicks him off a building; pilots his starfighter Xanadu Blood.
records.continuity: The Clone Wars 'Holocron Heist'; The Bad Batch 'Bounty Lost'
records.limitation: Rocket boots are short boosts, not sustained flight

records.name: Captain Rex
records.note: Wookieepedia/databank pages for Rex could not be fetched; the Y-wing escape with Ahsoka (Clone Wars S7) does not say who flew. No confirmed piloting scene.

records.name: Asajj Ventress
records.note: Canon text shows her receiving Nightsister magick (healing ritual, invisibility ichor enchanted by Talzin) but not casting it herself.

records.name: Savage Opress
records.note: Transformed by Mother Talzin's magicks and controlled by them; nothing shows him casting magick himself.

records.name: Jango Fett
records.feat: Databank lists a flamethrower among his weapons (Attack of the Clones).
records.note: weapon flamethrower; needs designer ruling whether this is commanding fire

records.name: Boba Fett
records.feat: Wrist gauntlet carries a mini flamethrower.
records.note: weapon flamethrower; needs designer ruling whether this is commanding fire

records.name: The Mandalorian
records.feat: Uses his vambrace flamethrower on Jawas, a stormtrooper, and reptavians (Chapters 2, 3, 7).
records.note: weapon flamethrower; needs designer ruling whether this is commanding fire

records.name: Leia Organa
records.feat: After the Raddus bridge is destroyed she drifts in space and uses the Force to move herself back to the cruiser.

records.name: Sabine Wren
records.feat: Uses her connection to the Force to call her lightsaber to her hand despite having no natural Force aptitude.

records.name: Darth Maul
records.feat: After Obi-Wan cut him in half he survived and built spider-like mechanical legs, later replaced with humanoid cybernetic legs.

records.name: Cad Bane
records.feat: Electro gauntlets with flamethrowers, stunners and remote ship controls, breathing tubes that defeat Force chokes, rocket boots, hypnogazer and knockout gas.
records.continuity: The Clone Wars; The Bad Batch; The Book of Boba Fett

records.name: Fennec Shand
records.feat: After being gut-shot, Boba Fett saves her life by having the interior of her lower abdomen replaced with cybernetics.
records.continuity: The Mandalorian 'Chapter 14: The Tragedy' (shown in The Book of Boba Fett)

records.name: Moff Gideon
records.feat: Flies an outland TIE fighter in the attack on Nevarro until Din Djarin brings it down.

records.name: Savage Opress
records.feat: Pilots a Punworcca 116-class sloop as Dooku's apprentice and later a hijacked Turtle Tanker to Lotho Minor.

records.name: Black Widow
records.feat: In Captain America: The Winter Soldier she sneaks aboard the pirate-held Lemurian Star to download S.H.I.E.L.D. files, and later uses a Photostatic Veil disguise to infiltrate the World Security Council. In The Avengers she approaches Loki's cell undetected.
records.continuity: MCU: The Avengers (2012); Captain America: The Winter Soldier (2014)

records.name: Hawkeye
records.note: Role only, no stealth feat found. The MCU sources list marksmanship, martial arts and piloting, not stealth. The closest moments are sniper perches (Thor, The Avengers) and letting the Tracksuit Mafia capture him (Hawkeye ep. 2), which is the opposite of stealth. Wikipedia's MCU article and the marvel.com ep. 2 recap were also checked. 'Vent Clint' is fan lore, not on screen.

records.name: Winter Soldier
records.feat: In The Winter Soldier he is so elusive that spies and assassins treat him as a myth, a 'ghost story'. After the D.C. highway fight he slips away from the scene unnoticed. He also staged the Starks' 1991 killing to look like a car accident.
records.continuity: MCU: Captain America: The Winter Soldier (2014); Captain America: Civil War (2016)
records.note: Earth-199999 is the Marvel Database's MCU continuity page; only film-sourced events were used.

records.name: Gamora
records.continuity: MCU: Guardians of the Galaxy films
records.note: Role only, no stealth feat found. Her Abilities section has no stealth entry. Her Orb 'surprise' theft at the Broker's turns into an open fight, and the Dark Aster raid is an open assault with the team. Wikipedia mentions that Thanos taught her 'stealth techniques', but that is training, not an on-screen feat.

records.name: Nebula
records.feat: In Infinity War she sneaks aboard Thanos's ship Sanctuary II to kill him and nearly succeeds before being caught. In Endgame, 2014 Nebula impersonates her future self to slip into 2023.
records.continuity: MCU: Avengers: Infinity War (2018); Avengers: Endgame (2019)

records.name: Nakia
records.feat: In Black Panther she goes undercover inside a kidnapped group in Nigeria (the wiki says she 'flawlessly' infiltrated a kidnapping). She also infiltrates Killmonger's farm to steal a Heart-Shaped Herb and leaves the City of the Dead without being noticed.

records.name: Yelena Belova
records.feat: In Black Widow (2021), after slipping her restraints, she creeps through the Red Room, knocking out guards while she searches for the Red Dust vials. She also gets into Natasha's old Budapest apartment and waits there for her.

records.name: Sharon Carter
records.feat: In The Winter Soldier, on Fury's orders, she lives across the hall from Steve Rogers posing as a nurse named 'Kate' and secretly watches him. In Civil War she secretly gets Captain America's shield and the Falcon gear to Rogers's fugitive team.
records.continuity: MCU: Captain America: The Winter Soldier (2014); Captain America: Civil War (2016)
records.note: Borderline: the feat is undercover cover-identity work, not physical concealment. Owner may prefer to treat cover-identity-only feats as insufficient.

records.name: Nick Fury
records.feat: In Captain Marvel he lifts an official's fingerprint with tape to get into the Project Pegasus facility and secretly pages his contact while inside. In The Winter Soldier he escapes the Winter Soldier through a hole cut under his car into the sewers, then fakes his death and hides.
records.continuity: MCU: Captain Marvel (2019); Captain America: The Winter Soldier (2014)

records.name: Elektra
records.feat: In Daredevil S2E6 'Regrets Only' she brings Matt into a Roxxon black-tie gala. They slip into a restricted area, she opens a hidden vault to steal the ledger, and they escape the guards with a fake drunken make-out.
records.note: Netflix Daredevil counts as MCU only if the roster accepts it (Marvel now lists it in the MCU timeline).

records.name: Valentina Allegra de Fontaine
records.continuity: MCU: The Falcon and the Winter Soldier; Black Widow; Thunderbolts*
records.note: Role only, no stealth feat found. On screen she operates openly (approaching John Walker on a bench, visiting him later). The only infiltration mentioned (Madame Hydra) comes from the comics, which do not count.

records.name: Bullseye
records.note: Role only, no stealth feat found. Sources show him attacking openly (the Bulletin fight while dressed as Daredevil, which is a disguise, not concealment) and long-range marksmanship. No sneaking or infiltration feat was documented.

records.name: Leonardo
records.feat: 'Karai's Vendetta' opens with the Turtles sneaking into an undersea Kraang lab, part of what the recap calls their habit of sneaking into Kraang labs. Leo orders silence inside, and he, Raph and Mikey pedal the Turtle Sub to keep its approach quiet.
records.continuity: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (2012 series) S1E21 'Karai's Vendetta'

records.name: Donatello
records.feat: Takes part in the Turtles' sneak into an undersea Kraang lab in 'Karai's Vendetta', though his ringing T-Phone nearly gives them away. In the 2003 series ('The Search for Splinter, Part 1') he fools TCRI's security cameras with a pigeon puppet during the break-in.
records.continuity: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (2012 series) S1E21 'Karai's Vendetta'; TMNT (2003) S1E25

records.name: Raphael
records.feat: One of the Turtles who sneak into an undersea Kraang lab in 'Karai's Vendetta'. He pedals the Turtle Sub to keep its approach quiet.
records.continuity: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (2012 series) S1E21 'Karai's Vendetta'

records.name: Michelangelo
records.feat: One of the Turtles who sneak into an undersea Kraang lab in 'Karai's Vendetta'. He pedals the Turtle Sub to keep its approach quiet.
records.continuity: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (2012 series) S1E21 'Karai's Vendetta'

records.name: Master Splinter
records.note: Only general descriptions were found: the 2012 wiki credits his stealth to speed ('get past his enemies like Dogpound') and says he lived 'in the shadows'. The 2003 Turtlepedia page shows him teaching 'ninjutsu powers of stealth and secrecy' and sensing invisible foes. No specific scene of him sneaking or infiltrating was found. The 1987 and 2012 Turtlepedia Splinter pages could not be fetched. Leaning toward 'role (sensei) only' unless a scene turns up.

records.name: Raiden
records.feat: As the main playable character of Metal Gear Solid 2 ('Tactical Espionage Action'), he sneaks through the Big Shell. He avoids detection by hanging from walkways to slip past guards, distracting them with thrown objects and shooting out their radios.
records.continuity: Metal Gear Solid 2: Sons of Liberty (2001)

records.name: Ezio Auditore
records.feat: Assassin's Creed II is built around Ezio's stealth. He blends into any crowd, hides underwater to break line of sight, distracts guards with tossed coins and hired courtesans or thieves, and makes hidden-blade assassinations.

records.name: Altaïr
records.feat: Assassin's Creed uses social stealth: Altaïr blends into crowds, hides in haystacks and rooftop gardens to shake guards, and makes low-profile Hidden Blade assassinations after eavesdropping and pickpocketing scouting missions.

records.name: Scorpion
records.note: Role only (ninja), no stealth feat found. His closest move, the Teleport Punch, is a teleport and is already covered by the teleport tag.

records.name: Widowmaker
records.note: Role only (assassin/sniper), no stealth feat found. Her kit (Widow's Kiss, Grappling Hook, Venom Mine, Infra-Sight) has no cloak. In lore, Sombra handles the infiltration ('Infiltration'), alarms go off, and in 'Alive' Tracer is waiting for her. The wiki gives the Stealth ability to Sombra.

records.name: Asajj Ventress
records.feat: In The Clone Wars ('Nightsisters') she and two sisters step into Mother Talzin's enchanted ichor, become nearly invisible, and crawl through the Serenno palace ducts to reach Dooku unseen. Earlier she slips through the Republic cruiser Tranquility's ventilation ducts to plant detonators.
records.limitation: Invisibility comes from Talzin's enchanted ichor, not her own power
records.note: The Wookieepedia text cites by reference number. The episode names are matched from the plot ('Nightsisters' S3E12; Tranquility = 'Cloak of Darkness' S1E9) and should be spot-checked.

records.name: Cassian Andor
records.feat: On Scarif in Rogue One he ambushes three Imperial officers, takes their uniforms and infiltrates the base with Jyn and K-2SO. On Eadu he watches Krennic's meeting unseen from a sniper perch. In Andor he joins the Aldhani heist undercover as 'Clem'.

records.name: Boba Fett
records.feat: In The Empire Strikes Back he hides among the Star Destroyer's dumped waste to secretly track the Millennium Falcon. In The Clone Wars he sneaks aboard the cruiser Endurance disguised as clone cadet 'Lucky' and plants a bomb.
records.continuity: The Empire Strikes Back; The Clone Wars

records.name: The Mandalorian
records.feat: In 'Chapter 15: The Believer' he and Mayfeld hijack an Imperial juggernaut, put on the Imperial uniforms, and drive into the Morak refinery unchallenged, with troopers saluting them. They are exposed only when Din must remove his helmet for a face scan.
records.note: Borderline: disguise-and-bluff, not unseen sneaking. His Chapter 3 compound raid is a loud breach. If disguise does not count, this becomes needs-research.

records.name: Fennec Shand
records.feat: In The Book of Boba Fett 'Chapter 7: In the Name of Honor' she slips into the Pykes' guarded hideout and kills nine people in about a minute, showing herself only once on purpose. She then hangs Mayor Mok Shaiz and stabs the Pyke boss in the back. TV Tropes files this under Stealth Expert.
records.continuity: The Book of Boba Fett 'Chapter 7: In the Name of Honor'

records.name: Bo-Katan Kryze
records.continuity: The Clone Wars; Rebels; The Mandalorian
records.note: Not found. Her Wookieepedia arsenal is WESTAR-35 pistols, dart launchers, gauntlet blades and a grappling line, with no flamethrower. The Flamethrower and ZX flame projector articles list Jango, Boba, Gar Saxon, Cad Bane and others but not her (the ZX article names her only as the person fighting Saxon). Her thrown explosives are not described as incendiary. Leaning toward rejected.

records.name: Sabine Wren
records.note: Not found. Her full Wookieepedia article shows explosives (thermal paint, thermal detonators, smoke grenades, blowing up an AT-DP) but no flamethrower or fire use. The Flamethrower article does not list her. Explosions are not commanding fire, so leaning toward rejected.

records.name: Death Trooper
records.feat: Death trooper armor goes beyond standard plating. The helmet has a Neuro-Saav macromotion monitor, multi-frequency targeting and acquisition sensors, and image-intensifying pulse emitters that give 'total situational awareness'. The armor also has a reflec polymer coating that warps sensor signals for stealth ops, and voice scramblers that only other death troopers can decode.
records.note: The capabilities are documented, but the article does not show a scene where a trooper depends on them. The starwars.com databank page could not be fetched.

records.name: Captain Phasma
records.continuity: The Force Awakens; The Last Jedi; Phasma (novel)
records.note: No advanced capabilities documented. Her armor is stormtrooper-style armor forged from salvaged chromium, which reflects radiation and deflects weak bolts but 'served primarily as a symbol'. There are no sensors or powered systems, so it fails the owner's ruling. Leaning toward rejected.

records.name: Stormtrooper
records.note: The canon armor does list a HUD, an integrated comlink, motion sensors, vision processing for darkness and smoke, air filtration and a temperature-regulating body glove. But this is standard rank-and-file kit, which the owner ruled a poor fit, and no on-screen reliance was found. Leaning toward rejected.

records.name: Marcus Fenix
records.note: The Gears wiki calls COG armor a 'personal body protection system' with a power pack for ID lights and helmet filters. It lists no strength assist, HUD, sensors or comms, so it is standard-issue armor and fails the armor ruling. Untested alternative: his use of the Hammer of Dawn targeting device (an orbital weapon) might qualify as a signature gadget. This was not researched here.

records.name: Sweetums
records.note: No documented height. Muppet Wiki only says he 'towers above his human and Muppet co-stars'. The Muppet Key Substack profile and searches for 'feet tall' turned up no measurement.

records.name: Mr. Snuffleupagus
records.note: No documented height. Documented size facts: he weighs 1,000 lb (Episode 1606), wears a 65 triple-G shoe, and the costume needs two performers and must be stored hung from the ceiling. Grunge, Mental Floss and Dictionary.com give no height either; Grunge gives a 6-ft minimum for the performer, not the character.

records.name: Big Mean Carl
records.note: No documented height. ToughPigs calls him 'massive', a 'gigantic messy creature' and a 'giant monster', which are qualitative only.

records.name: The Watcher
records.note: No documented height. The Wikipedia MCU article gives no size or scale. An earlier pass found the same on the MCU wiki (Uatu). Would need an on-screen scale scene.

records.name: Donkey Kong
records.note: No documented height. Super Mario Wiki gives only his weight, 800 lb (363 kg), from Donkey Kong 64's talking Microphone, plus 'big, tall, with lots of muscles'. Other Kongs (Chunky, Sumo) are larger. If no height turns up, the current giants grant is doubtful (see the earlier games dispute).

disputes.name: The Thing
disputes.note: In Fantastic Four: First Steps (2025) Ben Grimm is a bulky rock man of roughly human height, not giant. The official Hot Toys 1/6-scale figure is ~31.5 cm, about 6 ft 2 in at full scale (my calculation). No source describes him as giant or growing.

disputes.name: Vision
disputes.note: Weak. The MCU wiki lists no telepathy/telekinesis/mind control for Mind Stone Vision (only density shifting, flight, Mind Stone beams, and hacking Ultron by touch). The only mind-power evidence is WandaVision ep. 5, where the Hex Vision (Wanda's creation, no Mind Stone) uses Mind-Stone-like energy on Norm's temples to break Wanda's control. Keep only if that version counts.

disputes.name: Echo
disputes.note: Sources conflict. GamesRadar says the healing power belonged to Maya's mother and that Maya's touch sends Kingpin into a traumatic memory (not healing). Nerdist says the power can 'heal herself and others' but cites no on-screen healing. I found no scene of Maya physically healing anyone.

disputes.name: Ego
disputes.note: Low confidence. The MCU wiki Ego page describes no flight or levitation (only tethering to his ship with tendrils in space). Needs a specific scene, or recast as piloting if his egg-shaped ship counts.

disputes.name: Garfield
disputes.note: Unsupported. The rationale is a stereotype ('cat stealth when motivated'), not a feat; sources describe him as lazy, cynical and sarcastic with no stealth trait. Remove unless a specific strip or episode feat is found.

disputes.name: Frozone
disputes.note: Not true flight. The Disney Wiki describes 'limited airborne mobility, not necessarily complete levitation': he skates on self-made ice paths that hold up for only a short distance. He has no gliding, piloting or hovering. Keep ice; drop flight, or make it an explicit owner exception.

disputes.name: Popeye
disputes.note: Unsupported. Sources describe spinach only as a source of strength (Famous Studios formula, 'How Green Is My Spinach'). No healing or regeneration is described; 'cartoon regeneration' is a stereotype.

disputes.name: Sandy Cheeks
disputes.note: Low priority, probably keep with a limitation. She lives and fights underwater in Bikini Bottom, but she is a land squirrel who needs her oxygen suit and helmet (or the treedome) to breathe. Suggested limitation: 'Requires air suit/helmet underwater'.

disputes.name: Donkey Kong
disputes.note: Super Mario Wiki describes him as a burly ~800 lb gorilla. It never calls him giant-sized and gives no growth feat; other Kongs (Chunky) are bigger. Big, but not giant.

disputes.name: Scorpion
disputes.note: Wikipedia's character article describes him only as a ninja. It gives no stealth or invisibility feat, and 'ninja' alone is a job title. His real powers are teleport and fire.

disputes.name: Ganondorf
disputes.note: Borderline. Zelda Wiki shows him teleporting Zelda to himself in Ocarina of Time but no self-teleport. Keep only if teleporting others counts.

disputes.name: Widowmaker
disputes.note: Borderline. Overwatch Wiki lists no stealth or cloak ability (Infra-Sight reveals enemies), only lore training in 'covert arts' as an assassin. Close to a job-title grant.

disputes.name: Mr. Mime
disputes.note: Unsupported. Every Pokédex entry says Mr. Mime creates invisible walls/objects by miming; none says Mr. Mime itself becomes invisible, hides or is stealthy. The grant came from the roster blurb 'Invisible-wall performer'.

disputes.name: Magneton
disputes.note: Unsupported so far: no Magneton Pokédex entry mentions floating/hovering/anti-gravity, and Magneton does not have Levitate. Only its pre-evolution Magnemite has hover text. Keep only if designer accepts inheritance from Magnemite or another source is found (Bulbapedia refused fetch).

disputes.name: Weezing
disputes.note: Weakly supported: no Weezing Pokédex entry mentions floating; the only support is its Levitate ability, described in Sun/Moon onward as 'By floating in the air...'. Not wrong, but cite the ability rather than Pokédex text.

disputes.name: IG-88
disputes.note: No stealth feat found; StarWars.com databank describes him only as a battered chrome war droid turned bounty hunter. Likely a bounty-hunter stereotype.

disputes.name: Emperor Palpatine
disputes.note: Not a wrong grant but a missing one: Shock Troopers campaign matches 'Palpatine'/'Darth Sidious' while roster name is 'Emperor Palpatine', so a canonical lightning user is rejected.

disputes.name: Hawkeye
disputes.note: Currently granted; role only under the new ruling. See followup.json.

disputes.name: Gamora
disputes.note: Currently granted; no on-screen stealth feat (open ambush and assault only).

disputes.name: Valentina Allegra de Fontaine
disputes.note: Currently granted; no MCU stealth feat. The infiltration is from the comics only.

disputes.name: Bullseye
disputes.note: Currently granted; no stealth feat documented, only open attacks and marksmanship.

disputes.name: Scorpion
disputes.note: Currently granted; ninja title only.

disputes.name: Widowmaker
disputes.note: Currently granted; no cloak in her kit, and her lore missions are not stealthy.

disputes.name: Master Splinter
disputes.note: Currently granted; only general sensei/'lives in shadows' descriptions, with no specific feat found (needs-research).

disputes.name: Donkey Kong
disputes.note: Currently granted; no documented height (800 lb only). Fails the ~8 ft rule until a height is found.
